decisions.claim: B is a customer/diner at a restaurant
decisions.reason: George's statement 'I'll be your waiter this evening' presupposes B is a customer/diner at a restaurant. Solid E1 presupposition.
'before your meal' uses definite possessive 'your meal', presupposing B is having a meal. Solid E1.
'I'll be back in a minute with your drink' uses definite possessive 'your drink', presupposing B ordered a drink. Solid E1.
'with your drink and salad' uses definite possessive 'your salad', presupposing B ordered a salad. Solid E1.

decisions.claim: The interaction takes place in the evening
decisions.reason: 'this evening' explicitly states the time of the interaction. Valid E1 fact about B's dining situation.

decisions.claim: B is a customer at a restaurant being served by George
decisions.reason: c6 is a more complete restatement of c1 (customer at restaurant served by George). c1 already captures the core presupposition; c6 adds no new independent attribute beyond what c1 establishes.

decisions.claim: B is dining in the evening
decisions.reason: c7 ('B is dining in the evening') is equivalent to combining c1 (dining) + c5 (evening). It adds no new information beyond those two already-kept claims.

decisions.claim: B has a meal (main course) ordered or planned
decisions.reason: c8 ('B has a meal ordered or planned') is equivalent to c2 ('B is having a meal'). The parenthetical 'ordered or planned' adds no new information beyond the presupposition already captured.
c9 is identical in content to c3 ('B has ordered a drink'). Both cite the same evidence and make the same claim.
c10 is identical in content to c4 ('B has ordered a salad'). Both cite the same evidence and make the same claim.

decisions.claim: B ordered a salad, likely as an appetizer
decisions.reason: Second-review support: Turn 7 uses the definite possessive 'your salad,' which establishes that B ordered a salad. The core fact (B ordered a salad) is firmly established. The 'likely as an appetizer' qualifier is speculative (the salad could be a side or part of a main), but it does not undermine the established fact of the salad order itself.
decisions.counterexample: B could have ordered the salad as a side dish rather than an appetizer, but the salad order itself is confirmed.

decisions.claim: B was not ready to order at the initial greeting
decisions.reason: The question 'Are you ready to order or do you need a few more minutes?' does NOT establish that B was not ready. It is a neutral question offering both options. No answer from B is visible. Inferring B's state from the mere presence of the question is speculative.
decisions.counterexample: B could have been ready to order immediately; the question is standard waiter protocol.
